tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: Post office savings schemes are run by the _____ and are very safe because they are _____:
options: Department of Posts; backed by the Government of India (sovereign guarantee)

questions.question_text: Small savings interest rates are notified:
options: By the Ministry of Finance every quarter

questions.question_text: A common feature of post office schemes is:
options: Safety, fixed returns, nominal minimum deposits and nomination facility
questions.explanation: They are accessible in rural areas.

questions.question_text: The Post Office Savings Account has a minimum balance of:
questions.explanation: Interest is paid annually and cheque/ATM facility is available.

questions.question_text: The Post Office RD has a tenure of:
options: 5 years, with a minimum of Rs 100 per month

questions.question_text: The Post Office TD is available for tenures of:
The Monthly Income Scheme has a maximum investment of:
questions.explanation: It is a 5-year scheme paying monthly interest.

questions.question_text: Kisan Vikas Patra doubles the investment in about:
questions.explanation: It has no 80C benefit and no TDS.

questions.question_text: NSC VIII issue is a:
options: 5-year certificate with Section 80C deduction on the investment
questions.explanation: Interest is compounded annually and paid at maturity.

questions.question_text: PPF has a tenure of:
options: 15 years (extendable in blocks of 5 years), with Rs 500 minimum and Rs 1.5 lakh maximum per year

questions.question_text: EEE status means:
options: Exempt on investment, exempt on interest and exempt on maturity

questions.question_text: In PPF, loan is available from the:
options: 3rd to the 6th year, and partial withdrawal from the 7th year

questions.question_text: The Senior Citizen Savings Scheme is for:
options: Those aged 60 and above (and retired employees aged 55–60 under conditions)

questions.question_text: The maximum investment in SCSS is _____ and the tenure is _____:
questions.explanation: It has 80C benefit; interest is taxable.

questions.question_text: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is:
options: A savings scheme for the girl child

questions.question_text: SSY is for a girl below _____, with deposits for _____ and maturity at _____ from opening:
questions.explanation: Partial withdrawal of 50% is allowed at 18.

questions.question_text: SSY was launched under the campaign:
The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate was:
options: A 2-year scheme for women and girls, closed for new deposits after 31 March 2025

questions.question_text: Among PPF, NSC, SCSS and SSY, the one with a 21-year tenure is:
questions.explanation: PPF has 15 years; NSC and SCSS have 5.

questions.question_text: India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) was launched in:
questions.explanation: It is a payments bank wholly owned by the government.

questions.question_text: IPPB offers doorstep banking through:
options: Postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks with micro-ATMs

questions.question_text: An e-money order is:
options: The electronic version of the traditional postal money order
questions.explanation: A money order is a traditional postal remittance.

questions.question_text: India Post's international money transfer service is offered:
options: For inward remittances via Western Union

questions.question_text: AI detects fraud in postal accounts by:
options: Real-time monitoring of unusual transaction patterns
questions.explanation: E.g., sudden withdrawals or dormant account activity.

questions.question_text: Biometrics and OTP secure postal transactions by:
options: Verifying that the genuine customer is making the transaction

tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Jeevan Pramaan is:
options: A digital life certificate for pensioners, including face authentication
questions.explanation: It saves pensioners a visit to the office.

questions.question_text: A challenge in securing rural postal banking is:
options: Low digital literacy, poor connectivity and legacy systems

questions.question_text: The types of provident funds include:
The EPF operates under the _____ and is managed by _____:
questions.explanation: It applies to establishments with 20 or more employees.

questions.question_text: The EPF contribution rates are:
options: 12% of basic wages plus DA by the employee and 12% by the employer

questions.question_text: Of the employer's 12%, EPS gets _____ and EPF gets _____:
questions.explanation: EPS is on a wage ceiling of Rs 15,000.

questions.question_text: UAN is:
options: Universal Account Number that identifies an EPF member

questions.question_text: The EPF interest rate is declared by:
options: The Central Board of Trustees (approved by the Finance Ministry)

questions.question_text: Full EPF withdrawal is allowed at retirement (58 years) or:
questions.explanation: Partial withdrawals are allowed for marriage, education, illness and housing.

questions.question_text: A Voluntary Provident Fund is:
options: An extra contribution beyond 12% that earns the same EPF rate

questions.question_text: EPF differs from PPF in that EPF is:
options: For salaried employees with employer contributions, while PPF is open to all residents

questions.question_text: GPF is:
options: The General Provident Fund for government employees
questions.explanation: Those joining after 2004 are under NPS.

questions.question_text: EPFO invests mainly in:
options: Government securities, state development loans, PSU bonds and AAA corporate bonds
questions.explanation: It also invests in equity ETFs.

questions.question_text: Up to _____ of PF money can be invested in equity ETFs:
The growth of PF in India is shown by EPFO having:
options: Over 7 crore active contributors and a corpus of over Rs 25 lakh crore
questions.explanation: Digitisation through UAN and UMANG helped.

questions.question_text: EDLI is:
options: The Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance scheme providing life cover to EPF members
questions.explanation: It pays a lump sum to nominees.

questions.question_text: The EPS is:
options: The Employees' Pension Scheme, which provides pension after retirement from the employer's share
questions.explanation: 8.33% of the employer's share goes to it.

questions.question_text: The pillars of the pension system are:
options: Mandatory (EPF/EPS), voluntary (NPS, PPF) and social assistance (NSAP, APY)

questions.question_text: The NPS is regulated by:
questions.explanation: It was launched in 2004 for government employees and extended to all in 2009.

questions.question_text: NPS Tier I is _____ and Tier II is _____:
options: Mandatory, locked till 60; voluntary with flexible withdrawal
questions.explanation: Tier II is like a savings account.

questions.question_text: PRAN is:
options: Permanent Retirement Account Number of an NPS subscriber

questions.question_text: The asset classes in NPS are:
options: E (equity), C (corporate bonds), G (government securities) and A (alternative)

questions.question_text: NPS active choice means:
options: The subscriber decides the allocation, while auto choice follows a life-cycle fund
questions.explanation: Auto choice shifts from equity to debt with age.

questions.question_text: On NPS exit at 60, subscribers:
options: Use a portion to buy an annuity and take the rest as a lump sum (rules revised from time to time)

questions.question_text: Tax benefits of NPS include:
options: 80CCD(1), an additional Rs 50,000 under 80CCD(1B) and employer's contribution under 80CCD(2)
questions.explanation: 80CCD(2) is also available in the new regime.

tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: The Unified Pension Scheme is:
options: An option for government employees from 1 April 2025 alongside NPS, with an assured payout on 25+ years of service

questions.question_text: The Atal Pension Yojana is:
options: A scheme for unorganised-sector workers aged 18–40, with a guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000–5,000 from age 60

questions.question_text: The Old Pension Scheme (OPS) is:
options: A defined-benefit pension for government employees who joined before 2004
questions.explanation: The pension is fixed by formula.

questions.question_text: A defined benefit pension differs from a defined contribution pension in that DB:
options: Pays a fixed amount by formula, while DC depends on contributions and returns
questions.explanation: OPS is DB; NPS is DC.

questions.question_text: An annuity is:
options: A series of regular payments, usually purchased with a lump sum to provide pension

questions.question_text: Longevity risk is:
options: The risk of outliving one's savings
questions.explanation: It is a key retirement risk.

questions.question_text: AI helps in personalised pension planning by:
options: Computing the required corpus, recommending contributions and asset allocation

questions.question_text: The retirement corpus is calculated from:
options: Expenses × inflation × years in retirement (with expected returns)
questions.explanation: The result is the amount needed at retirement.

questions.question_text: A Monte Carlo simulation in retirement planning:
options: Runs many random scenarios of returns to estimate the chance of meeting goals
questions.explanation: It shows the probability of success.

questions.question_text: A challenge in pension investments is:
options: Longevity and inflation risks, low contributions and market volatility

questions.question_text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act:
questions.explanation: The notes use the 1961 section numbers.

questions.question_text: The new tax regime is:
options: The default regime with lower slab rates and fewer deductions, while the old regime has higher rates but allows deductions

questions.question_text: Section 80C eligible investments include:
options: EPF, PPF, NSC, SSY, tax-saver FD and ELSS
questions.explanation: Also life insurance premium and home-loan principal.

questions.question_text: The limit of Section 80C is:
The 80C instrument with the shortest lock-in is:
The lock-in period of ELSS is:
questions.explanation: It is the shortest among 80C options.

questions.question_text: Section 80CCD(1B) provides:
options: An additional deduction of up to Rs 50,000 for NPS contributions

questions.question_text: Section 80D allows deduction for:
options: Health insurance premium: Rs 25,000 for self, spouse and children plus Rs 25,000 for parents
questions.explanation: Limits are higher for senior citizens.

questions.question_text: The 80D limit for senior citizens is:
questions.explanation: It applies to self or parents who are senior citizens.

questions.question_text: Section 80G allows deduction for:
options: Donations: 100% or 50% of the amount, with or without a qualifying limit (10% of adjusted gross income)

questions.question_text: A cash donation of Rs 5,000 under 80G is:
options: Not eligible, since cash donations above Rs 2,000 are not allowed
questions.explanation: Donations should be by non-cash modes.

questions.question_text: Section 80E gives deduction for:
options: Interest on education loan, with no upper limit for 8 years

questions.question_text: Section 80TTA allows deduction up to _____ on savings account interest, and 80TTB gives _____ for senior citizens:
One must file an ITR if:
options: Income exceeds the basic exemption limit or in other specified cases
questions.explanation: Also for foreign assets and high deposits.

questions.question_text: The due date for filing ITR for non-audit individuals is:
questions.explanation: Belated returns are allowed with fees.

tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: ITR-1 (Sahaj) is for:
options: Residents with salary, one house property and other sources up to Rs 50 lakh
questions.explanation: ITR-2 is for capital gains and ITR-4 for presumptive income.

questions.question_text: Form 16 is:
options: A TDS certificate issued by the employer for salary

questions.question_text: Form 26AS, AIS and TIS show:
options: The taxpayer's tax credits and financial transactions reported to the tax department
questions.explanation: They are used to verify the return.

questions.question_text: A belated return is:
options: A return filed after the due date

questions.question_text: A revised return is:
options: A return filed to correct errors in the original return

questions.question_text: e-Verification of an ITR must be done within:
Ways of e-verification include:
options: Aadhaar OTP, net banking, EVC and DSC
questions.explanation: One can also send a signed ITR-V to CPC Bengaluru.

questions.question_text: To file ITR using an Excel utility, one first:
options: Downloads the utility from the e-filing portal for the relevant ITR form and assessment year
questions.explanation: Then fill, validate and generate the JSON file.

questions.question_text: The JSON file in e-filing is:
options: The file generated by the utility that is uploaded to the portal to file the return
questions.explanation: It is uploaded in offline mode.

questions.question_text: Taxable income is calculated as:
The 4% cess is:
options: Health and education cess added to the tax payable
questions.explanation: It is levied on tax plus surcharge.

questions.question_text: The Section 87A rebate:
options: Reduces tax payable for resident individuals with income below a specified limit
questions.explanation: It can bring tax to zero.

questions.question_text: Gross income Rs 8 lakh, 80C Rs 1.5 lakh, 80D Rs 25,000 (old regime). The taxable income is:
One should prefer small savings schemes because they:
options: Are safe and give assured returns, but their limitations are lower returns and limits

questions.question_text: Three post office schemes with 80C benefit are:
options: NSC, 5-year TD and SSY (or PPF and SCSS)
questions.explanation: KVP, MIS and RD have no 80C benefit.

questions.question_text: KVP differs from NSC in that KVP:
options: Doubles the investment in a fixed period with no 80C benefit, while NSC is a 5-year certificate with 80C benefit
questions.explanation: Both have a minimum of Rs 1,000.

questions.question_text: MIS differs from SCSS in that MIS:
options: Pays monthly interest with no age limit, while SCSS pays quarterly interest for seniors with 80C benefit

questions.question_text: A dormant account is:
options: An account with no transactions for a long period; it is reactivated by completing KYC and a transaction
questions.explanation: Unclaimed balances go to the DEA Fund after 10 years.

questions.question_text: TDS on interest can be avoided if the depositor submits:
options: Form 15G (below the taxable limit) or Form 15H (senior citizens)
questions.explanation: They declare that no tax is payable.

questions.question_text: PPF Rs 1,000 per year for 3 years at 7% (annual compounding, deposits at start of year) matures at about:
Form 15G differs from Form 15H in that 15G is for:
options: Individuals below 60, and 15H for senior citizens aged 60 and above

questions.question_text: A pensioner submits a digital life certificate through:
options: Jeevan Pramaan using Aadhaar biometrics or face authentication

questions.question_text: Section 80C differs from 80CCD(1B) in that 80CCD(1B) gives:
options: An additional Rs 50,000 deduction only for NPS beyond the 80C limit

questions.question_text: Small savings schemes are called sovereign-guaranteed because:
options: They are backed by the Government of India

questions.question_text: PPF partial withdrawal is allowed:
options: From the 7th year, limited to a prescribed percentage of the balance
questions.explanation: Full withdrawal is only at maturity.
